# Results — Study 299 (Keynote-Drift) on AAPL daily prices

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Apple keynote dates are
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../keynote_drift/data.py) (2008–2025, 48 events). AAPL daily
adjusted closes (price-only, split/dividend-adjusted via yfinance `auto_adjust=True`)
are cached at `_cache/aapl_daily.parquet`. Match the fingerprint below to confirm you
hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| AAPL daily adjusted close (price-only, yfinance) | 2007-06-01 → 2025-12-30 | 4,676 trading days | `bc084ab781e7` |
| Apple keynote table | 2008–2025 (WWDC / September / Spring) | 48 events | hardcoded constant |

## The honest benchmark — AAPL against itself

AAPL rose roughly 50x over 2008–2025. *Any* short window has a positive average
return, so the only meaningful test measures keynote-window returns **in excess
of AAPL's own unconditional daily mean** (a constant-mean market model). This is
the abnormal return; without it you merely rediscover that AAPL went up. The
common mistake in "buy the rumor" write-ups is to point at the raw run-up and
call it a keynote effect.

## Event study — pre/post cumulative abnormal returns (CARs)

| Window | Mean abnormal CAR | t-stat | p-value | permutation p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-keynote (5 trading days before reveal) | **−0.193%** | −0.387 | 0.7007 | 0.7539 |
| Post-keynote (reveal day + 4) | **−1.121%** | −1.729 | 0.0904 | — |

- **Pre-keynote ("buy the rumor"):** mean abnormal CAR −0.19%, t = −0.39,
  permutation p = 0.75. The observed mean sits in the dead centre of a
  random-anchor null. **There is no abnormal run-up into Apple keynotes.**
- **Post-keynote ("sell the news"):** mean abnormal CAR −1.12%, t = −1.73,
  p = 0.09. Suggestive of a mild post-event droop but **short of the |t| ≥ 2
  evidence bar**, and (see below) not robust on any subset.

## Slicing by event type and sub-period

| Slice | Mean pre-keynote abnormal CAR |
|---|--:|
| WWDC (n=18) | +0.94% |
| Spring (n=11) | +0.80% |
| September (n=19) | −1.84% |
| Early (≤2016) | −0.347% |
| Late (≥2017) | −0.083% |

The post-event droop concentrates in September iPhone events, but on that subset
(n=19) the **post-keynote CAR is −1.33% with t = −1.10, p = 0.287** — not
significant. The pre-keynote drift is near zero in both the early and late
sub-periods. No robust pocket of signal survives slicing.

## The n = 48 problem (power)

With 48 single-name events and a per-event CAR standard deviation of ~3.46%, the
minimum detectable mean CAR at 80% power (two-sided, α = 0.05) is:

    MDE ≈ (t_crit + t_power) · 3.46% / √48 ≈ 1.43%/event

The observed pre-keynote CAR is −0.19% — about **13% of the detection
threshold**. Even the September post-event droop (−1.33%) is below the bar on its
own subset. n = 48 cannot resolve a sub-1.4%/event drift.

## Could you trade it?

The tradable "buy the rumor" leg: long AAPL from 5 trading days before each
keynote (one trading-day execution lag), exit at the event-eve close, pay 5 bps
one-way × NAV (10 bps round trip), price-only.

| Metric | Gross | Net (10 bps round trip) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean return per trade | +0.519% | +0.419% |
| Hit-rate | 58.3% | — |
| Total compounded (48 events) | +24.9% | +19.1% |
| Trade frequency | ~2.8 events/yr | — |

The leg is **net-positive — but it captures only AAPL's ordinary ~4-day drift**
(the abnormal CAR is zero). You take concentrated single-name gap risk a few
times a year to harvest what buy-and-hold gives you for free. There is no keynote
alpha to capture.

## Positive control

A synthetic AAPL tape with a planted keynote drift confirms the event-study
machinery works: at a planted drift of ~50 bps/day the detected pre-keynote CAR
clears t ≥ 2 with permutation p < 0.05; the null (0 bps) reproduces the −0.19%
flat result seen on the real tape. The null is a statement about **AAPL and
sample size**, not about the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Pre-keynote abnormal CAR −0.19%, t = −0.39, permutation
  p = 0.75. The post-event droop (t = −1.73) is suggestive but does not clear the
  |t| ≥ 2 bar and is non-significant on the September subset. No robust keynote
  drift survives benchmarking AAPL against itself.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "buy the rumor" trade nets ~0.4%/event, which is
  AAPL's own multi-day drift — not a keynote edge — earned with concentrated
  single-name risk while out of the market most of the year.
- **Busted — a great stock's trend, mistaken for a calendar omen.** The folklore
  confuses AAPL's 2008–2025 secular uptrend with a keynote effect; the abnormal
  (de-trended) windows are flat.
